summary:
SURVEY OF MEMORY SYSTEMS AND HOW EACH HANDLES STORAGE, UPDATES, AND VALIDITY/STALENESS/SUPERSESSION.

(1) MemGPT/Letta (arXiv 2310.08560; docs.letta.com). OS-inspired "virtual context management" with three tiers: core memory (editable in-context blocks, e.g. persona/human), recall memory (searchable out-of-context conversation history), and archival memory (vector-DB table for long-term facts/documents). The agent SELF-manages memory via tool calls (core_memory_append/replace, archival_memory_insert/search): updates happen only when the LLM decides to rewrite a core block or insert into archival memory. Validity handling: essentially none beyond ad-hoc overwriting — there is no temporal model, no supersession semantics, and stale archival entries persist forever and can be retrieved alongside newer contradicting ones; contradiction resolution is left entirely to the generating LLM. Reported numbers: MemGPT scores 93.4% on the Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR) benchmark (as reported in the Zep paper for comparison).

(2) Mem0 / Mem0g (arXiv 2504.19413, Apr 2025). Two-phase pipeline: an extraction phase distills candidate facts from new conversation turns; an update phase retrieves the top-s semantically similar existing memories and has an LLM pick one of four operations: ADD (no equivalent exists), UPDATE (augment existing), DELETE (remove memories contradicted by new information), NOOP. This is explicit contradiction resolution, but it is DESTRUCTIVE and WRITE-TIME: a contradicted old memory is deleted globally, even though it might be exactly what a historical question needs. Mem0g stores directed labeled graphs (entities as nodes, relations as edges) and, on conflict, marks obsolete relations invalid rather than hard-deleting. Notably, Mem0's platform v3 migration notes state the newer algorithm "only adds new facts" (no UPDATE/DELETE at extraction) — an industry retreat from destructive write-time resolution. Numbers (LoCoMo, LLM-as-Judge): Mem0 66.9%–67.13% vs OpenAI Memory 52.9% (26% relative uplift); Mem0g best on temporal questions 58.13% vs OpenAI 21.71%; p95 search latency ~0.20s; ~90% fewer tokens than full-context (~1,764 vs 26,031 per conversation).

(3) Zep / Graphiti (arXiv 2501.13956, Jan 2025). Temporally-aware knowledge graph engine with three subgraphs: episodic (raw messages), semantic entity (extracted entities/relations), and community. THE key prior art for QVF's temporal story: a BI-TEMPORAL model with four timestamps per fact/edge — t_created/t_expired (transaction/ingestion timeline) and valid_at/invalid_at (real-world validity timeline). On ingestion, new edges are compared by an LLM against semantically related existing edges; if superseded, the old edge is INVALIDATED (expired_at/invalid_at set) but NOT deleted, preserving history so agents can answer "what was true last Tuesday". Temporal logic over the dual timeline determines fact validity at any query time. Crucially, though, the supersession decision is made ONCE, globally, at write time — it is not re-derived per query. Numbers: DMR 94.8% (gpt-4-turbo) vs MemGPT 93.4%, 98.2% with gpt-4o-mini; LongMemEval accuracy improvements up to 18.5% over a full-context baseline with ~90% latency reduction; secondary sources cite ~71.2% overall LongMemEval and 63.8% on the temporal-retrieval subtask.

(4) A-MEM (arXiv 2502.12110; NeurIPS 2025). Zettelkasten-inspired atomic "memory notes" with LLM-generated contextual description, keywords, tags, plus embeddings. On adding a note, the system runs link generation (bidirectional links to nearest neighbors) and MEMORY EVOLUTION: an LLM prompt decides whether the new note should trigger rewriting of neighboring notes' context/tags. There is NO deletion and no explicit contradiction/supersession/temporal semantics — conflicting notes coexist; any "validity" emerges implicitly if evolution happens to rewrite a neighbor's text. Evaluated on LoCoMo with gains especially on multi-hop questions over MemGPT/MemoryBank/ReadAgent baselines.

(5) HippoRAG (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2405.14831) and HippoRAG 2 (ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.14802, "From RAG to Memory"). HippoRAG: OpenIE extracts triples into a schema-less KG with synonym edges (hippocampal index); retrieval runs Personalized PageRank seeded from query entities (pattern completion), enabling single-step multi-hop. HippoRAG 2 adds deeper passage integration (passages as nodes), query-to-triple linking, and an LLM "recognition memory" filter for seed selection; framed as NON-PARAMETRIC CONTINUAL LEARNING — new knowledge is appended and connected. Validity handling: none — the graph is append-only; contradictory triples coexist with no timestamps, no invalidation, no staleness model. Numbers: HippoRAG 2 beats the best embedding model (NV-Embed-v2) by ~7% on associative (multi-hop) memory tasks with stronger factual and sense-making performance.

(6) MemoryBank (AAAI 2024, arXiv 2305.10250). Hierarchical store: raw turns, daily event summaries, and evolving user-personality summaries; powers the SiliconFriend companion. Update mechanism: an EBBINGHAUS FORGETTING CURVE-inspired decay — each memory has a strength that is reinforced when retrieved and decays with elapsed time, so old unretrieved memories are forgotten/deleted. This is a purely time/recency-based GLOBAL staleness heuristic: no contradiction detection, no supersession semantics, and it can delete old facts that would still be valid for historical queries — the exact failure mode QVF's query-conditioned framing targets.

(7) MemoChat (arXiv 2308.08239, 2023). Tuning/instruction pipeline teaching LLMs an iterative memorization–retrieval–response loop over self-composed STRUCTURED MEMOS (topic-organized summaries of dialogue segments). Consistency comes from re-retrieving memos; memos are appended, not revised — no update, invalidation, temporal scoping, or contradiction machinery. Evaluated on a manually annotated long-range consistency test set (MT-Bench+ style), not LongMemEval/LoCoMo.

(8) Reflexion (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv 2303.11366). Episodic memory of verbal self-reflections: after a failed trial, the agent generates a natural-language self-critique stored in a bounded episodic buffer (typically 1–3 reflections) prepended to later attempts. Memory is task-scoped and reset between tasks; "staleness" is handled only by the sliding-window bound. No validity or contradiction reasoning — but it seeded the paradigm of textual, LLM-written memory artifacts that A-MEM/Mem0 build on.

(9) NOTABLE 2025–2026 SYSTEMS. MemOS (arXiv 2507.03724): treats memory as a first-class OS resource via MemCube encapsulation of parametric/activation/plaintext memory with lifecycle governance (provenance, versioning, access control, transitions between memory types); LoCoMo overall LLM-judge 73.31→75.80 (MemOS-1031) vs MIRIX 64.33 and Mem0 59.22; 159% temporal-reasoning improvement over OpenAI memory; 2026 marketing claims 88.83 LoCoMo / 89.20 LongMemEval. MemoryOS (EMNLP 2025 Oral, arXiv 2506.06326): short/mid/long-term hierarchical storage; short→mid via dialogue-chain FIFO, mid→long via segmented paging with HEAT-based promotion/eviction — updates are recency/heat-driven overwrites, no semantic conflict resolution; LoCoMo +48.36% F1 avg over baselines (GPT-4o-mini). MIRIX (arXiv 2507.07957): six memory stores (core, episodic, semantic, procedural, resource, knowledge-vault) each managed by a dedicated agent plus a router; multimodal/screen capture; 85.38% avg on LoCoMo (claims >8 pts over LangMem/Mem0). Memory-R1 (arXiv 2508.19828): RL (PPO/GRPO) fine-tunes a Memory Manager for {ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, NOOP} and an Answer Agent that performs MEMORY DISTILLATION — retrieving up to 60 candidates and filtering to the relevant subset before answering; with only 152 training QA pairs it beats Mem0 on LoCoMo by +48% F1/+69% BLEU-1/+37% LLM-judge (LLaMA-3.1-8B) and generalizes to MSC and LongMemEval; its Answer Agent is the closest RL-based analog to a post-retrieval filter, but it emits no structured, interpretable validity artifact. LightMem (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.18866): Atkinson-Shiffrin-inspired sensory buffer → topic-aware short-term memory → SLEEP-TIME offline long-term consolidation (update decoupled from inference); LongMemEval +2.09–6.40% (GPT) with up to 38x token reduction. SeCom (ICLR 2025, arXiv 2502.05589, Microsoft): segment-level memory granularity plus LLMLingua-2 compression as retrieval denoising; gains on LoCoMo and Long-MT-Bench+. MemInsight (EMNLP 2025, arXiv 2503.21760, Amazon): autonomous attribute-based memory augmentation/annotation; +34% recall over RAG baseline on LoCoMo retrieval. M+ (ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.00592): latent-space memory pool (MemoryLLM) plus co-trained retriever, extending retention from <20k to >160k tokens — parametric rather than symbolic, so validity is inapplicable. Hindsight (arXiv 2512.12818, vectorize.io): four networks (World, Experience, Opinion, Entity/Observation) with retain/recall/reflect operations; reports 91.4% overall on LongMemEval (claimed SOTA as of early 2026). EverMemOS (ACL 2026): self-organizing memory OS for long-horizon reasoning.

(10) DIRECTLY QVF-ADJACENT 2026 WORK (validity/supersession as the research object). STALE benchmark (arXiv 2605.06527): "Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid?" — 400 expert-validated implicit-conflict scenarios (co-referential vs propagated conflicts), 1,200 queries, contexts to 150K tokens; probes State Resolution, Premise Resistance, Implicit Policy Adaptation; best frontier model (Gemini-3.1-pro) only 55.2% overall; models at 92% on direct questions collapse to ~30% under stale-premise queries; memory frameworks evaluated (LightMem, Zep, LiCoMemory, A-MEM, Mem0) do poorly; their CUPMem prototype (write-side state adjudication) reaches 68%. TOKI (arXiv 2606.06240): bitemporal operator algebra (valid time + transaction time) with formal supersession/contradiction-resolution/temporal-composition operators for agent memory. "Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory" / MemStrata (arXiv 2606.26511): deterministic (subject, relation, object) supersession layer retiring stale values in a bi-temporal ledger, arguing plain RAG cannot eliminate stale-fact errors by construction. MOSAIC (reported in that literature): 66% contradiction detection at ingestion vs 2–14% for existing memory systems. "Beyond Dialogue Time: Temporal Semantic Memory for Personalized LLM Agents" (arXiv 2601.07468). These confirm the problem QVF targets is recognized as open in 2026 — but ALL of these place the resolution machinery at WRITE/ingestion time or in a deterministic ledger, not as a query-conditioned read-time semantic analysis.

papers.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems (now Letta)
papers.core_idea: Virtual context management: self-editing core memory blocks in-context, recall memory (conversation DB) and archival memory (vector DB) out-of-context, all managed by the agent via tool calls.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Establishes agent-managed memory but has zero validity machinery: no timestamps semantics, no supersession, stale archival entries coexist with new ones. QVF would sit between its retrieval calls and generation; MemGPT is a system QVF could wrap, not a competitor on validity.

papers.title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
papers.core_idea: Extraction + update pipeline where an LLM chooses ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP against retrieved similar memories; Mem0g graph variant marks obsolete relations invalid; LoCoMo J 66.9% vs OpenAI 52.9%, p95 search 0.20s.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Closest write-time contradiction resolver. Key difference: Mem0 resolves conflicts DESTRUCTIVELY and GLOBALLY at ingestion (DELETE), losing history that a historical query needs; QVF keeps all memories and judges validity per query at read time. Mem0's own v3 retreat to add-only implicitly concedes the write-time-deletion problem.

papers.title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory (Graphiti)
papers.core_idea: Bi-temporal knowledge graph: every edge carries transaction-time (created_at/expired_at) and valid-time (valid_at/invalid_at); new contradictory facts invalidate (not delete) superseded edges; DMR 94.8%, LongMemEval up to +18.5% acc with 90% lower latency.
papers.relation_to_qvf: The strongest prior art for temporal scoping. Differences: (a) invalidation is decided once at WRITE time by an ingestion LLM, not re-derived per query; (b) validity is a global property of the edge, whereas QVF's labels (HISTORICAL_FOR_QUERY etc.) are query-conditioned; (c) Zep outputs a graph, not an interpretable claims/relations/roles/sufficiency map with citations.

papers.title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
papers.core_idea: Zettelkasten-style atomic notes (context, keywords, tags, embedding) with LLM-driven link generation and memory evolution that rewrites neighboring notes' descriptions when new notes arrive.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Append-only with soft evolution; no contradiction/supersession/temporal semantics — conflicting notes silently coexist. Its 'evolution' mutates memory content (write-time), whereas QVF leaves memories untouched and produces an external validity map. A-MEM is a natural baseline memory backend for QVF experiments.

papers.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for LLMs
papers.core_idea: OpenIE-built KG as hippocampal index + Personalized PageRank from query entities for single-step multi-hop retrieval across documents.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Pure retrieval-side association; append-only, no timestamps, no invalidation — contradictory triples coexist. Orthogonal to QVF: it improves WHAT is retrieved, QVF judges what retrieved items MEAN for the query.

papers.title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for LLMs (HippoRAG 2)
papers.core_idea: Enhances HippoRAG with passage nodes, query-to-triple linking, and an LLM recognition-memory filter for PPR seeds; +7% on associative memory over best embedding retrievers; frames RAG-as-continual-learning.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Despite the 'continual learning' framing, knowledge integration is pure appending — no staleness, conflict, or temporal validity handling at all. Demonstrates that even SOTA 'memory' RAG leaves the validity problem entirely to the reader LLM, which is exactly the slot QVF fills.

papers.title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
papers.core_idea: Hierarchical store (turns, daily event summaries, personality portraits) with an Ebbinghaus forgetting-curve update rule: memory strength reinforced on retrieval, decays/deletes with elapsed time.
papers.relation_to_qvf: The canonical example of GLOBAL time-based staleness: old = weak = forgotten. QVF's core thesis is the direct rebuttal — an old memory can be exactly right for a historical question; recency-decay deletes it. Excellent contrast baseline in the paper's related work.

papers.title: MemoChat: Tuning LLMs to Use Memos for Consistent Long-Range Open-Domain Conversation
papers.core_idea: Instruction-tuned memorization–retrieval–response loop over self-written structured topical memos for long-range consistency.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Structured memory artifacts, but write-once summaries with no update/invalidation/temporal scoping; consistency depends on retrieval hitting the right memo. Shows early structured-memo lineage that QVF's Validity Map generalizes into a typed, query-conditioned analysis.

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.core_idea: Episodic buffer of natural-language self-reflections generated after failures, bounded sliding window, prepended to subsequent trials — verbal RL without weight updates.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Origin of textual episodic memory for agents; task-scoped, reset per task, no validity reasoning. Relevant only as lineage; its bounded-buffer 'forgetting' is another global recency heuristic QVF replaces with per-query judgment.

papers.title: MemOS: A Memory OS for AI System
papers.core_idea: MemCube abstraction unifying parametric/activation/plaintext memory with lifecycle governance (provenance, versioning, scheduling); LoCoMo LLM-judge 73.31–75.80, 159% temporal-reasoning gain over OpenAI memory.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Governance/versioning metadata exists but conflict handling is infrastructural (versions, provenance), not semantic; no query-conditioned applicability or relation typing between memories. QVF could be positioned as the missing semantic 'validity layer' such OS-style systems lack.

papers.title: Memory OS of AI Agent (MemoryOS)
papers.core_idea: Short/mid/long-term hierarchical storage with dialogue-chain FIFO and heat-based segmented paging for promotion/eviction; LoCoMo +48.36% F1 over baselines on GPT-4o-mini.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Updates are recency/heat-driven overwrites — again a global, content-blind staleness policy with no contradiction semantics; superseded info is evicted rather than temporally scoped.

papers.title: MIRIX: Multi-Agent Memory System for LLM-Based Agents
papers.core_idea: Six typed memory stores (core, episodic, semantic, procedural, resource, knowledge-vault), each with a manager agent plus a query router; multimodal screen-capture memory; 85.38% avg on LoCoMo.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Typed STORES but not typed RELATIONS between memories; each manager decides what belongs in its store — no cross-memory contradiction/supersession analysis and no query-time validity labels.

papers.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing LLM Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
papers.core_idea: PPO/GRPO-trained Memory Manager ({ADD,UPDATE,DELETE,NOOP}) plus an Answer Agent that distills up to 60 retrieved memories down to a relevant subset; with 152 training QAs beats Mem0 by +48% F1/+69% BLEU-1/+37% J on LoCoMo; generalizes to MSC and LongMemEval.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Nearest neighbor to QVF's post-retrieval filtering slot: its Answer Agent filters retrieved memories before answering. But it is a learned opaque filter — no atomic claims, no relation labels, no temporal/applicability labels, no sufficiency/abstention output, and its Memory Manager still does destructive write-time ops. QVF's differentiator: structured, interpretable, query-conditioned validity map with citations.

papers.title: LightMem: Lightweight and Efficient Memory-Augmented Generation
papers.core_idea: Atkinson-Shiffrin pipeline: sensory-buffer compression → topic-aware short-term memory → sleep-time offline long-term consolidation; LongMemEval +2.09–6.40% (GPT) with up to 38x fewer tokens.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Consolidation (including conflict merging) is offline and global ('sleep-time'), decoupled from any specific query; evaluated by STALE as still failing implicit-invalidation cases.

papers.title: SeCom: On Memory Construction and Retrieval for Personalized Conversational Agents
papers.core_idea: Segment-level memory granularity (topical segmentation) plus LLMLingua-2 compression as denoising; beats turn/session/summary granularities on LoCoMo and Long-MT-Bench+.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Purely granularity/compression work; no validity dimension. Useful as evidence that raw retrieved memory is noisy — QVF addresses the semantic noise (invalid/contradictory/distractor) rather than the token noise.

papers.title: MemInsight: Autonomous Memory Augmentation for LLM Agents
papers.core_idea: LLM autonomously mines attributes to annotate/structure stored memories, improving retrieval; +34% recall over RAG baseline on LoCoMo retrieval.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Write-time semantic enrichment of individual memories; no inter-memory relations, no query-conditioned judgments. QVF's Validity Map is the read-time, relational counterpart.

papers.title: M+: Extending MemoryLLM with Scalable Long-Term Memory
papers.core_idea: Latent-space memory pool with a co-trained retriever, extending retention from <20k to >160k tokens.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Parametric/latent memory line — validity, citation, and contradiction are not even expressible; cite to delimit QVF's scope to symbolic/textual memory.

papers.title: Hindsight: Building Agent Memory that Retains, Recalls, and Reflects
papers.core_idea: Four memory networks (World, Experience, Opinion, Entity/Observation) with retain/recall/reflect ops; reports 91.4% overall LongMemEval, claimed SOTA early 2026.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Current LongMemEval leader to beat/compare; separates opinion vs world facts but does not emit query-conditioned validity/temporal labels.

papers.title: STALE: Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid?
papers.core_idea: Benchmark of 400 implicit-conflict scenarios / 1,200 queries (co-referential vs propagated conflicts, contexts to 150K tokens) probing state resolution, premise resistance, and implicit policy adaptation; best model 55.2%; memory frameworks (LightMem, Zep, LiCoMemory, A-MEM, Mem0) fare poorly; CUPMem write-side adjudication reaches 68%.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Strongest evidence the QVF problem is open and hard: even 2026 frontier models fail implicit invalidation, and premise-embedded stale queries crater accuracy 92%→30%. STALE's CUPMem fixes it at WRITE time; QVF's read-time query-conditioned map is the untried alternative. STALE could be an additional evaluation target for QVF beyond LongMemEval/LoCoMo.

papers.title: TOKI: A Bitemporal Operator Algebra for Contradiction Resolution in LLM-Agent Persistent Memory
papers.core_idea: Formal algebra over valid-time × transaction-time coordinates with supersession, contradiction-resolution, and temporal-composition operators for agent memory.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Formalizes bi-temporal supersession as deterministic algebra; QVF differs by treating validity as a query-conditioned SEMANTIC judgment (an LLM adapter emitting typed labels), covering relations TOKI cannot express (COMPLEMENTS, QUALIFIER, DISTRACTOR, sufficiency, risk flags).

papers.title: Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory: Eliminating Stale-Fact Errors for AI Agents (MemStrata)
papers.core_idea: Deterministic (subject, relation, object) supersession rule retiring stale values in a bi-temporal ledger; argues plain RAG cannot eliminate stale-fact errors by construction; reports large contradiction-detection gaps in existing systems (2–14% vs MOSAIC-style 66% at ingestion).
papers.relation_to_qvf: Same problem, opposite mechanism: deterministic write-time ledger vs QVF's read-time LLM semantic analysis. QVF's counterargument: (s,r,o) matching misses paraphrase/conditional/partial conflicts and cannot express 'valid for THIS historical query'.

papers.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
papers.core_idea: 500 manually created questions over long chat histories testing five abilities: information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, abstention; commercial systems only 30–70%; temporal-aware designs gain 7–11% on temporal reasoning.
papers.relation_to_qvf: QVF's main evaluation. Its knowledge-update, temporal-reasoning, and abstention subtasks map one-to-one onto QVF's SUPERSEDED_FOR_QUERY/temporal labels and SUFFICIENT/INSUFFICIENT assessment.

sota_numbers: DMR: Zep 94.8% (gpt-4-turbo) / 98.2% (gpt-4o-mini) vs MemGPT 93.4% (arxiv.org/abs/2501.13956). LongMemEval: Zep up to +18.5% acc over full-context with 90% latency cut, ~71.2% overall and 63.8% temporal-retrieval per secondary sources (blog.getzep.com, baeseokjae.github.io/posts/zep-ai-agent-memory-review-2026); Hindsight 91.4% overall, claimed SOTA early 2026 (arxiv.org/pdf/2512.12818, vectorize.io); LightMem +2.09–6.40% acc (GPT) with up to 38x token reduction (arxiv.org/abs/2510.18866); MemOS claims 89.20 (github.com/MemTensor/MemOS, 2026); commercial assistants only 30–70% per original paper (arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813). LoCoMo (LLM-as-Judge unless noted): Mem0 66.9–67.13 vs OpenAI Memory 52.9, Mem0g temporal 58.13 vs 21.71, p95 search 0.20s (arxiv.org/abs/2504.19413, mem0.ai/research-3); MIRIX 85.38 (arxiv.org/abs/2507.07957); MemOS 73.31→75.80 (MemOS-1031) vs MIRIX 64.33, Mem0 59.22, +159% temporal vs OpenAI memory (arxiv.org/abs/2507.03724, github.com/MemTensor/MemOS); MemoryOS +48.36% F1 avg over baselines on GPT-4o-mini (arxiv.org/abs/2506.06326); Memory-R1 (LLaMA-3.1-8B GRPO) +48% F1 / +69% BLEU-1 / +37% J over Mem0 (arxiv.org/abs/2508.19828); MemInsight +34% recall over RAG on LoCoMo retrieval (arxiv.org/abs/2503.21760). Validity-specific: STALE best frontier model 55.2% overall, direct-question 92% → 30% under stale premises, CUPMem 68% (arxiv.org/html/2605.06527v1); contradiction detection at ingestion 2–14% for existing systems vs 66% for MOSAIC-style adjudication (arxiv.org/html/2606.26511). HippoRAG 2: +7% associative memory over NV-Embed-v2 (arxiv.org/abs/2502.14802).
benchmark_details: This area is a systems survey, but the two planned QVF benchmarks recur throughout: LongMemEval (ICLR 2025): 500 questions, five ability types (single/multi-session information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, abstention); variants LongMemEval-S (~115k-token histories) and LongMemEval-M (~500 sessions / up to ~1.5M tokens); JSON with question, answer, question_type, question_date, haystack_sessions (timestamped turn lists), answer_session_ids; official metric is LLM-judged QA accuracy per type plus abstention; judge scripts in the official repo. LoCoMo (Maharana et al. 2024): 10 very long multi-session conversations (~600 dialogues, ~26k tokens each, session timestamps), ~1,540–2,000 QA pairs in categories single-hop, multi-hop, temporal, open-domain/world-knowledge (and adversarial/unanswerable in the original); community practice (Mem0 paper) evaluates with F1/BLEU-1 plus LLM-as-a-Judge 'J' score; note category-numbering discrepancies across papers when comparing.
download_info: LongMemEval: github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval (official, ICLR 2025) — data files longmemeval_s.json, longmemeval_m.json, longmemeval_oracle.json via the repo's HuggingFace/Google Drive links (huggingface.co/datasets/xiaowu0162/longmemeval). LoCoMo: github.com/snap-research/locomo (official) — locomo10.json plus evaluation scripts; Mem0's evaluation harness for LoCoMo at github.com/mem0ai/mem0 (evaluation directory). STALE benchmark (optional third eval): arxiv.org/html/2605.06527v1 (repo linked from paper).
gaps_for_qvf: Six concrete gaps QVF can claim. (1) Write-time vs read-time: every surveyed system that handles conflict at all does it at INGESTION — Mem0 deletes, Memory-R1's manager updates/deletes, Zep/Graphiti and TOKI/MemStrata set invalid_at once, CUPMem adjudicates on write, LightMem consolidates offline. No system re-derives validity conditioned on the current query at read time; Zep's bi-temporal graph can ANSWER historical queries but its supersession decision (later timestamp ⇒ invalidate) is global and irreversible per edge. QVF's query-conditioned labels (an old memory is CURRENT_FOR_QUERY for a historical question; a later timestamp alone does not prove supersession) occupy an empty slot. (2) No interpretable intermediate artifact: no system emits a structured map of atomic claims with memory-ID citations, typed inter-claim relations (EQUIVALENT/SUPPORTS/CONTRADICTS/SUPERSEDES/…), and per-memory roles between retrieval and generation — Memory-R1's Answer Agent filters opaquely; everything else passes raw text. (3) Append-only systems (A-MEM, HippoRAG 1/2, MemoChat, HippoRAG-style RAG generally) have zero contradiction semantics, so the reader LLM silently arbitrates conflicts — STALE shows even frontier models do this at ~55% and collapse to ~30% under stale-premise queries, quantifying the failure QVF prevents. (4) Recency-decay staleness (MemoryBank's Ebbinghaus curve, MemoryOS heat paging) deletes/evicts old-but-historically-valid memories — the exact anti-pattern QVF's thesis rebuts; use as motivating contrast. (5) Sufficiency and abstention: LongMemEval's abstention subtask is the weakest across reported systems, and no surveyed memory system performs explicit sufficiency assessment (SUFFICIENT/INSUFFICIENT/AMBIGUOUS) or risk flagging before generation. (6) Distractor labeling: no system identifies retrieved-but-misleading memories (QVF's DISTRACTOR/UNRESOLVED roles); benchmarks (LongMemEval haystacks, STALE distractor sessions) already contain the needed material, so QVF can quantify distractor identification as a novel metric. Evaluation positioning: LongMemEval knowledge-update + temporal-reasoning + abstention subsets and LoCoMo temporal/adversarial categories map directly onto QVF outputs, and STALE (2026) is an emerging third benchmark explicitly about memory invalidation where QVF's read-time approach can be contrasted with CUPMem's write-time adjudication.

summary:
This survey covers four intertwined threads from 2021-2026: (1) knowledge-conflict research (context-memory and inter-context), (2) temporal QA benchmarks, (3) temporal validity of facts as a research topic, and (4) mechanisms that decide WHICH evidence is valid for a given query time.

(1) Knowledge conflict. The field was seeded by Longpre et al. (EMNLP 2021), whose entity-substitution framework creates context-memory conflicts by replacing the answer entity in a gold passage with an alternate entity (same-type, alias, corpus, popularity variants); they found QA models over-rely on parametric memory, modulated by model size and entity popularity. Chen, Zhang & Choi (EMNLP 2022, "Rich Knowledge Sources Bring Complex Knowledge Conflicts") extended this to the realistic multi-passage setting (up to 100 retrieved passages + parametric knowledge), showing that contradictions among sources barely move model confidence, and proposed a calibration objective that discourages committing to a single answer when retrieved evidence contains multiple conflicting candidates. Xie et al. (ICLR 2024, "Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth") showed LLMs are highly receptive to coherent counter-memory evidence yet exhibit strong confirmation bias when any evidence agrees with their parametric belief. ClashEval (NeurIPS 2024 D&B) quantified the "tug-of-war": on 1,200+ questions with perturbed retrieved documents, LLMs adopt wrong retrieved content over 60% of the time, adoption probability falls as the perturbation becomes more implausible and rises when the model's prior token-probability confidence is low; they use these signals (prior vs. context probability comparison) as a simple conflict-resolution mechanism. Jin et al. (LREC-COLING 2024, "Tug-of-War Between Knowledge") found stronger RALMs show a Dunning-Kruger-like persistence in faulty internal memory. The EMNLP 2024 survey "Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs" established the now-standard taxonomy: context-memory, inter-context, and intra-memory conflict, cataloguing causes and mitigation families (faithful-to-context prompting, decoding-time interventions like context-aware decoding, disentanglement like DisentQA, fine-tuning like KAFT). ConflictBank (NeurIPS 2024 D&B) is the largest conflict benchmark (7.45M claim-evidence pairs, 553k QA pairs) explicitly covering misinformation, TEMPORAL, and semantic conflict causes. DynamicQA (Findings EMNLP 2024) showed temporally dynamic facts produce more intra-memory conflict and are HARDER to override with context - directly relevant to memory-augmented agents where the most frequently updated facts are the most conflict-prone. Behavioral studies with real (non-synthetic) documents (Kortukov et al. 2024) and task-dependence studies (2506.06485) refine the picture. Mechanism-level interventions include IRCAN (reweighting context-aware neurons), ParamMute (suppressing knowledge-critical FFNs), Micro-Act (actionable self-reasoning over conflicts), and proxy-model steering of context sensitivity (2508.19720).

(2) Inter-context conflict and conflict-aware RAG. Astute RAG (Google, 2410.07176) iteratively consolidates internal and external knowledge with source-awareness; in their study 70% of retrieved passages lacked a direct answer and 19.2% of instances had internal-external conflicts. RAMDocs/MADAM-RAG (2504.13079) simulates realistic mixtures of ambiguity, misinformation, and noise, and resolves them via per-document agents that debate plus an aggregator that distinguishes legitimate ambiguity (multiple valid answers) from misinformation - conceptually close to QVF's role labels but implemented as free-form debate, not a typed structured map. "Open Domain QA with Conflicting Contexts" (2410.12311) crowdsourced conflict annotations on Google-retrieved contexts (about 25% of real retrieved contexts conflict). Healthcare-focused work (2511.06668) highlights outdated recommendations and evolving consensus as the canonical inter-context conflict source.

(3) Temporal QA benchmarks. TimeQA (NeurIPS 2021 D&B; Chen et al.) built time-evolving facts from Wikidata with easy/hard implicit variants. TempLAMA (Dhingra et al., TACL 2022, "Time-Aware Language Models as Temporal Knowledge Bases") introduced temporally-scoped cloze queries and joint training with time prefixes; known biases: 2010-2020 span only and 70.69% of questions answered by the subject's most frequent object, encouraging frequency shortcuts. SituatedQA (2021) showed answers depend on temporal/geographic context of the asker. TempReason (ACL 2023) spans longer ranges and three reasoning levels (time-time, time-event, event-event), showing LLM accuracy collapses on low-resource years. MenatQA (Findings EMNLP 2023) probes scope, order, and counterfactual temporal factors. TIQ (WWW 2024 companion) targets implicit temporal constraints ("during the Cold War"). ChroKnowledge/ChroKnowBench (ICLR 2025) evaluates chronological knowledge across domains, distinguishing evolving vs. invariant facts and showing models partially recall or cut off at temporal boundaries; ChroKnowPrompt traverses neighboring years to elicit knowledge. Dynamic/live benchmarks: RealTimeQA, FreshQA/FreshLLMs (Findings ACL 2024; never/slow/fast-changing and false-premise categories; FreshPrompt), PAT-Questions (present-anchored, self-updating), UnSeenTimeQA (memorization-free), DyKnow (dynamically updated outdated-knowledge checks), EvolvingQA (NAACL 2024; continual-learning models fail at updating/removing outdated knowledge), GrowOVER (ACL 2024; RaLMs struggle with recently updated knowledge), DynaQuest, Test of Time (synthetic temporal-logic), TRAVELER (vague/implicit/explicit references), Complex-TR, TEMPO (2026, temporal-reasoning-intensive retrieval). The comprehensive survey "It's High Time: A Survey of Temporal Question Answering" (2505.20243) taxonomizes by source (diachronic news vs. Wikipedia snapshots), explicitness, and reasoning complexity, and lists open challenges: answer drift over static snapshots, temporal uncertainty ("all dates treated as exact"), implicit temporal intent, and weak robustness.

(4) Temporal alignment and temporal validity. "Time is Encoded in the Weights of Finetuned Language Models" (2312.13401) found linear yearly decay plus seasonal misalignment and introduced time vectors; "Set the Clock" (Findings ACL 2024) showed pretrained LMs hold a "chaotic" internal sense of time and can be aligned to a target year (even 2022 alignment improving over earlier years); Ticktack (2503.04150) uses sexagenary cycle encodings for long-range time; activation-engineering work (2505.14158) steers time-sensitive facts. Most striking for QVF: "Right Knowledge, Wrong Answer" (2606.20959, 2026) shows models often CONTAIN both the outdated and the newer fact but emit the outdated one (parametric temporal conflict); their Temporal Attractor Steering recovers 29-57% of conflict cases. Temporal validity as a text property is studied by Wenzel & Jatowt: Temporal Validity Change Prediction (Findings ACL 2024) benchmarks detecting context statements that change how long a statement remains valid; Chronocept (2505.07637) models validity as continuous probability curves over time. On the systems side, MemStrata (2606.26511, 2026, "Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory") is the closest system-level neighbor to QVF: a bi-temporal ledger with a deterministic supersession rule (same subject+relation, different object => retire older entry, no LLM call), motivated by an impossibility result that embedding similarity cannot separate contradictions from duplicates (AUROC 0.59, contradictions are MORE similar to originals than duplicates are); it achieves about 0% stale-fact errors vs. RAG's 15-40%, but supersession reliability drops from 97% on clean single-value facts to 44% on messy prose, and its supersession is GLOBAL (newer always retires older), not query-conditioned. "Question Answering under Temporal Conflict" (2506.07270) builds Temporal Wiki (Wikipedia snapshots) and Unified Clark (timestamped news) and shows an agentic structured external memory with temporal filtering beats ICL/RAG when multiple fact versions co-occur in context.

(5) How existing methods decide WHICH evidence is valid for a query time - mechanisms and limitations. Mechanism families found: (a) score fusion at retrieval: TempRALM ("It's About Time", 2401.13222) adds temporal relevance to Atlas retrieval (up to 74% over Atlas); recency priors with half-life decay (score = alpha*cos + (1-alpha)*0.5^(age/h)); timestamp-aware embeddings (TempRetriever, TsContriever); (b) query decomposition + rerank: TimeR4 (EMNLP 2024) retrieve-rewrite-retrieve-rerank grounds implicit time in TKG facts; MRAG (Findings EMNLP 2025) separates semantic from temporal relevance and is evaluated on TempRAGEval (manually perturbed time-sensitive questions with gold evidence); (c) hard temporal filtering / windowing (time-aware RAG pipelines that disentangle subject and temporal window); (d) version/structure-aware indexing: VersionRAG, DyG-RAG (event-centric dynamic graphs), RAG-meets-temporal-graphs (2510.13590), MemoTime, HALO (half-life-based outdated-fact filtering in TKGs), AionRAG; (e) deterministic supersession over structured memory (MemStrata); (f) LLM prior-vs-context arbitration using token probabilities (ClashEval) or self-consolidation (Astute RAG) or multi-agent debate (MADAM-RAG); (g) parametric interventions (temporal alignment, TAS steering). Documented limitations: recency heuristics are corpus-sensitive and fail silently - the Freshness study (2509.19376) shows optimal (alpha, half-life) on one corpus collapses to 0.00 Latest@10 on another, and narrow top-K semantic candidate selection discards the newest item before any recency prior can act; LLM rerankers exhibit systematic recency bias, promoting artificially newer timestamps by up to 95 ranks and reversing 25% of pairwise preferences even with identical content (2509.11353), which is exactly the "later timestamp proves supersession" fallacy QVF rejects; supersession-by-recency breaks on historical questions (temporal QA surveys note systems "treat all dates as exact" and cannot infer implicit query time); filtering approaches delete rather than label, losing evidence needed for historical/comparative queries; conflict-resolution approaches (debate, consolidation, calibration) output a single answer or abstention rather than an auditable per-claim validity structure; and almost all conflict benchmarks manufacture conflicts synthetically (entity substitution, perturbation), which recent work shows behaves differently from naturally occurring conflicts in real documents.

papers.title: Entity-Based Knowledge Conflicts in Question Answering
papers.core_idea: Creates context-memory conflicts by substituting the answer entity in gold passages (same-type/alias/corpus/popularity substitutions); shows QA models over-rely on parametric memory.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Foundational conflict-construction methodology; QVF differs by treating conflict as one of many typed relations (CONTRADICTS/SUPERSEDES/...) over real retrieved memories rather than synthetic substitutions, and by conditioning on the query.

papers.title: Rich Knowledge Sources Bring Complex Knowledge Conflicts: Recalibrating Models to Reflect Conflicting Evidence
papers.core_idea: Multi-passage + parametric conflicts barely change model confidence; proposes calibration that withholds a single answer under conflicting answer candidates.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Closest early precedent for QVF's sufficiency/AMBIGUOUS output; but it only calibrates confidence, without identifying which evidence is valid or why.

papers.title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of Large Language Models in Knowledge Conflicts
papers.core_idea: LLMs accept coherent counter-memory evidence yet show confirmation bias when any evidence matches parametric beliefs.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Motivates an explicit pre-generation validity map: implicit conflict handling inside the generator is biased; QVF externalizes it as auditable labels.

papers.title: ClashEval: Quantifying the tug-of-war between an LLM's internal prior and external evidence
papers.core_idea: 1,200+ questions with perturbed retrieved docs; LLMs adopt wrong context >60% of the time; adoption depends on perturbation plausibility and prior confidence; proposes token-probability arbitration.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Its arbitration mechanism is answer-level and probability-based; QVF instead produces claim-level, query-conditioned validity judgments with metadata-grounded reasons.

papers.title: Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey
papers.core_idea: Standard taxonomy: context-memory, inter-context, intra-memory conflict; catalogues causes, behaviors, and mitigations.
papers.relation_to_qvf: QVF's relation set refines 'inter-context conflict' into typed relations and adds query-conditioned temporal/applicability axes the survey identifies as open problems.

papers.title: Tug-of-War Between Knowledge: Exploring and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
papers.core_idea: Evaluation framework for internal-vs-external conflicts; stronger RALMs persistently favor faulty internal memory (Dunning-Kruger effect).
papers.relation_to_qvf: Evidence that resolution cannot be left to the generator; supports a dedicated pre-generation filter module.

papers.title: ConflictBank: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Influence of Knowledge Conflicts in LLMs
papers.core_idea: 7.45M claim-evidence pairs / 553k QA pairs covering misinformation, temporal, and semantic conflict causes.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Largest conflict benchmark including temporal conflicts; could supply auxiliary training/eval data for QVF's CONTRADICTS vs SUPERSEDES distinction.

papers.title: DynamicQA: Tracing Internal Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
papers.core_idea: Temporally dynamic and disputable facts cause more intra-memory conflict and are harder to update via context.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Shows the facts memory-augmented agents update most often are exactly the ones models resist updating - the failure mode QVF's UPDATE/SUPERSEDED labels target.

papers.title: Astute RAG: Overcoming Imperfect Retrieval Augmentation and Knowledge Conflicts for Large Language Models
papers.core_idea: Source-aware iterative consolidation of internal and external knowledge; finalizes answer by information reliability.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Consolidates into one answer without exposing structure; QVF outputs the intermediate validity map explicitly, enabling audit, abstention, and downstream control.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Conflicting Evidence (RAMDocs / MADAM-RAG)
papers.core_idea: RAMDocs mixes ambiguity, misinformation, noise, and imbalanced support; MADAM-RAG resolves via per-document agents debating plus an aggregator distinguishing legitimate ambiguity from misinformation.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Nearest inter-context-conflict method in spirit (distinguishes ambiguity from misinformation); QVF replaces expensive multi-round debate with a single typed structured map including temporal validity, which debate lacks.

papers.title: Open Domain Question Answering with Conflicting Contexts
papers.core_idea: Human-annotated naturally occurring conflicts in retrieved web contexts (~25% of questions); finetuning LLMs to explain conflict resolution helps.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Confirms natural conflicts are frequent and that explanation-style supervision helps - supports QVF's citation-bearing claims design.

papers.title: TimeQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering over Time-Evolving Facts
papers.core_idea: Wikidata-derived time-evolving facts with easy/hard (implicit) temporal specifications.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Canonical temporal-scope QA; but assumes a single gold answer per time scope and provides evidence already scoped - no notion of judging retrieved-memory validity.

papers.title: Time-Aware Language Models as Temporal Knowledge Bases (TempLAMA)
papers.core_idea: Temporally-scoped cloze probes; time-prefix training; documents frequency-shortcut bias (70.69% most-frequent-answer).
papers.relation_to_qvf: Shows parametric time-conditioning is weak; QVF instead conditions on query time at inference over external memories.

papers.title: Towards Benchmarking and Improving the Temporal Reasoning Capability of Large Language Models (TempReason)
papers.core_idea: Three-level temporal reasoning benchmark (time-time, time-event, event-event); accuracy collapses on low-resource years.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Benchmark for the reasoning QVF's temporal labels must encode; its time-sensitive RL fine-tuning is a parametric alternative to QVF's inference-time labeling.

papers.title: MenatQA: A New Dataset for Testing the Temporal Comprehension and Reasoning Abilities of Large Language Models
papers.core_idea: Probes scope, order, and counterfactual temporal factors, emphasizing implicit temporal information.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Its scope factor (question time narrower/wider than fact validity interval) is precisely QVF's PARTIALLY_APPLICABLE / temporal-label problem.

papers.title: TIQ: A Benchmark for Temporal Question Answering with Implicit Time Constraints
papers.core_idea: Auto-constructed questions whose time constraint is implicit via events/eras rather than explicit dates.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Shows query time is often not literal in the query - QVF's Semantic Adapter must infer the implied reference time before labeling validity.

papers.title: ChroKnowledge: Unveiling Chronological Knowledge of Language Models in Multiple Domains
papers.core_idea: ChroKnowBench separates time-variant vs invariant facts across domains; ChroKnowPrompt traverses neighboring years; models show partial recall/temporal boundary cutoffs.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Its evolving-vs-constant fact distinction parallels QVF's TIME_INSENSITIVE label; purely parametric evaluation, no retrieved-evidence filtering.

papers.title: FreshLLMs: Refreshing Large Language Models with Search Engine Augmentation (FreshQA)
papers.core_idea: FreshQA categorizes questions by answer volatility (never/slow/fast-changing, false-premise); FreshPrompt injects fresh search results.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Volatility categories inform QVF's temporal labels; FreshPrompt assumes newest search results are valid - the recency assumption QVF explicitly refuses.

papers.title: Time is Encoded in the Weights of Finetuned Language Models
papers.core_idea: Time vectors: temporal misalignment is linear-in-years with seasonal structure and manipulable via weight arithmetic.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Parametric temporal alignment is complementary; QVF handles per-query time conditioning that weight-space methods cannot.

papers.title: Set the Clock: Temporal Alignment of Pretrained Language Models
papers.core_idea: Pretrained LMs encode a chaotic sense of time; alignment methods can target a chosen year.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Aligns the model to ONE global time; QVF's premise is that validity must be conditioned per query, including historical query times.

papers.title: Right Knowledge, Wrong Answer: Test-Time Steering for Temporal Fact Conflicts in Open-Weight Language Models
papers.core_idea: Models retain both outdated and newer facts but emit the outdated one; Temporal Attractor Steering recovers 29-57% of conflict cases without retraining.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Parametric-side mirror of QVF's SUPERSEDES problem; activation steering always prefers the newer fact, so it cannot serve historical queries - QVF's query-conditioning is the differentiator.

papers.title: Temporal Validity Change Prediction
papers.core_idea: Task: detect context statements that change how long a target statement remains valid (Twitter-sourced dataset).
papers.relation_to_qvf: Establishes 'temporal validity' as an NLP property of statements; QVF operationalizes it as query-conditioned labels over retrieved memories rather than free-standing durations.

papers.title: Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory: Eliminating Stale-Fact Errors for AI Agents over Evolving Knowledge (MemStrata)
papers.core_idea: Bi-temporal ledger with deterministic supersession (same subject+relation, new object retires old entry; no LLM call); shows embedding similarity cannot separate contradictions from duplicates (AUROC 0.59); ~0% stale-fact errors vs RAG 15-40%.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Closest system to QVF. Key differences: supersession is global and recency-driven (newer always wins) vs QVF's query-conditioned validity (old memory can be CURRENT_FOR_QUERY for historical questions); drops to 44% reliability on messy prose, exactly where an LLM Semantic Adapter should win; QVF also adds relations, roles, sufficiency, risk flags.

papers.title: Question Answering under Temporal Conflict: Evaluating and Organizing Evolving Knowledge with LLMs
papers.core_idea: Temporal Wiki (Wikipedia snapshots) and Unified Clark (timestamped news) benchmarks; agentic structured external memory + temporal filtering beats ICL/RAG when multiple fact versions co-occur.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Validates structured memory organization for temporal conflict; its resolution is chronological filtering, not typed per-claim labels, and lacks applicability/sufficiency assessment.

papers.title: It's About Time: Incorporating Temporality in Retrieval Augmented Language Models (TempRALM)
papers.core_idea: Adds temporal relevance scoring to Atlas retrieval (up to 74% over baseline) without retraining.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Retrieval-stage temporal scoring; complements QVF, which sits after retrieval and judges validity rather than rank.

papers.title: TimeR4: Time-aware Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering
papers.core_idea: Retrieve-rewrite-retrieve-rerank pipeline grounding implicit temporal constraints in TKG facts, plus time-aware fine-tuned reranking.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Query-time grounding via rewriting is a useful sub-mechanism for QVF's adapter; restricted to structured TKGs, not free-form conversational memories.

papers.title: MRAG: A Modular Retrieval Framework for Time-Sensitive Question Answering (with TempRAGEval)
papers.core_idea: Separates semantic from temporal relevance; TempRAGEval adds temporal perturbations and gold-evidence labels for diagnostic evaluation.
papers.relation_to_qvf: TempRAGEval's diagnostic gold-evidence protocol is a model for evaluating QVF's per-memory labels; MRAG still scores relevance, not validity, and outputs no conflict structure.

papers.title: Freshness and the Limits of Heuristic Trend Detection in Temporal RAG
papers.core_idea: Half-life recency priors are extremely parameter- and corpus-sensitive (Latest@10 from 1.00 to 0.00); narrow top-K semantic candidate selection discards newest items before recency reranking can act.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Direct empirical evidence that recency heuristics cannot decide validity - supporting QVF's thesis that validity requires semantic, query-conditioned judgment.

papers.title: Do Large Language Models Favor Recent Content? A Study on Recency Bias in LLM-Based Reranking
papers.core_idea: All tested LLM rerankers systematically promote artificially newer timestamps with identical content (up to 95 ranks, 25% pairwise reversals); larger models attenuate but never eliminate the bias.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Quantifies the 'later timestamp = more valid' fallacy inside LLMs themselves; QVF must be designed (and evaluated) to resist this bias, e.g., via historical-query counterexamples.

papers.title: Carpe Diem: On the Evaluation of World Knowledge in Lifelong Language Models (EvolvingQA)
papers.core_idea: Continual-learning LMs on evolving Wikipedia fail specifically at updating and removing outdated answers.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Shows parametric updating fails at exactly the outdated-knowledge problem; supports inference-time validity filtering over external memory.

papers.title: DyKnow: Dynamically Verifying Time-Sensitive Factual Knowledge in LLMs
papers.core_idea: Queries Wikidata at evaluation time to check LLM answers against current ground truth, avoiding benchmark staleness.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Dynamic gold-truth protocol useful for QVF evaluation hygiene (checking adapter labels against live fact validity intervals).

papers.title: HALO: Half-Life Based Outdated Fact Filtering in Temporal Knowledge Graphs
papers.core_idea: Filters outdated TKG facts using estimated half-lives of relations.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Relation-level decay prior is a heuristic complement; global filtering again destroys evidence valid for historical queries, unlike QVF's labeling.

papers.title: It's High Time: A Survey of Temporal Question Answering
papers.core_idea: Comprehensive TQA survey: taxonomy, benchmarks (diachronic/synchronic/dynamic), temporal LMs vs temporal RAG; open challenges: answer drift, temporal uncertainty, implicit temporal intent.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Names the exact gaps QVF fills: systems treat dates as exact, cannot infer hidden timeframes, and handle retrieval and validity 'separately'.

papers.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
papers.core_idea: 500 questions testing information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, abstention over ~115k-token (S) / ~500-session (M) histories; long-context LLMs drop 30-60%.
papers.relation_to_qvf: QVF's planned main benchmark; its temporal-reasoning + knowledge-update + abstention categories map one-to-one onto QVF's temporal labels, SUPERSEDES relation, and SUFFICIENT/INSUFFICIENT output.

sota_numbers: ClashEval (NeurIPS 2024): LLMs override their own correct prior with wrong retrieved content >60% of the time; adoption falls with perturbation implausibility and rises with low prior confidence (https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10198). Astute RAG: 70% of retrieved passages lacked direct answers; 19.2% of instances had internal-external conflict, 47.4% of which were correctly resolved by internal knowledge alone; 84.45% TriviaQA / 62.24% BioASQ after 3 consolidation rounds (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07176). MADAM-RAG: +11.40% over strong RAG baselines on AmbigDocs, +15.80% absolute on FaithEval with Llama3.3-70B (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13079). MemStrata (2026): evolving-knowledge accuracy 0.95-1.00 vs RAG 0.20-0.47; stale-fact errors ~0% vs 15-40%; contradiction-vs-duplicate embedding separation AUROC 0.59; supersession reliability 97% (clean) vs 44% (messy prose) (https://arxiv.org/html/2606.26511). Recency-bias reranking (SIGIR-AP 2025): artificial fresh timestamps shift Top-10 mean publication year by up to +4.78 years, move items up to 95 ranks, reverse 25% of pairwise preferences (https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11353). TAS steering (2026): recovers 29-57% of parametric temporal-conflict cases while preserving 85-99% non-conflict accuracy on Qwen2.5/Mistral/Llama3.1 over an 8,746-record Wikidata benchmark (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20959). TempRALM: up to 74% improvement over Atlas baseline (https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.13222). Freshness study: Latest@10 swings 1.00 -> 0.00 across corpora for fixed recency-prior parameters; trend labeling only 0.08 macro-F1 with naive rules (https://arxiv.org/html/2509.19376). LongMemEval: long-context LLMs drop 30-60% on LongMemEval_S; commercial memory systems 30-70% accuracy (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813). TempLAMA bias: 70.69% of questions answered by subject's most frequent object (frequency shortcut) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08952 analysis).
benchmark_details: This area is primarily methods+benchmarks context (QVF's main eval benchmarks LongMemEval/LoCoMo are covered by a separate area), but key reusable resources: ConflictBank: 7.45M claim-evidence pairs, 553k QA pairs; three conflict causes (misinformation, temporal, semantic); QA-format probes for retrieved-knowledge conflict, encoded-knowledge conflict, and their interplay. RAMDocs: extends AmbigDocs-style multi-answer disambiguation with misinformation and noise documents and varying per-answer document support; expected output = all valid answers (ambiguity) while suppressing misinformation; metric = answer-set accuracy/F1. TempRAGEval: time-sensitive questions (repurposed from TimeQA/SituatedQA) with manual temporal perturbations and gold evidence annotations on Wikipedia; diagnostic metrics for retrieval (evidence recall) and end-to-end answer accuracy. ChroKnowBench: time-variant vs time-invariant triples across general/biomedical/legal/commonsense/math domains with year-stamped objects. DynamicQA: (s,r,o) Wikipedia facts over 16 relations flagged static/temporal/disputable, each paired with a conflicting substituted-answer snippet; measures semantic entropy and coherent-persuasion score. FreshQA: ~600 questions labeled never/slow/fast-changing/false-premise, answers refreshed regularly; two-mode human eval (Relaxed/Strict). MenatQA: 2,853 time-sensitive samples with scope/order/counterfactual factor perturbations. TimeQA: 41k question-passage pairs, easy/hard splits (explicit vs implicit time scope). Judge protocols in this literature are mostly exact-match/F1 for extractive benchmarks and LLM-as-judge or human eval for freshness benchmarks (FreshQA strict mode requires no outdated statements anywhere in the response - a protocol worth borrowing for QVF).
