gaps_for_qvf: Concrete gaps QVF can claim: (1) No existing method outputs a QUERY-CONDITIONED validity structure. Every surveyed mechanism either (a) filters/reranks at retrieval time (TempRALM, MRAG, TimeR4, HALO, half-life priors) - deleting or demoting evidence globally, which destroys memories that are valid for historical questions; (b) resolves to a single answer inside generation (Astute RAG consolidation, MADAM-RAG debate, ClashEval probability arbitration) - opaque, non-auditable, answer-level not claim-level; or (c) supersedes globally by recency (MemStrata's deterministic ledger, TAS steering toward newer facts) - hard-codes 'newer wins', the exact assumption QVF rejects. Nothing produces per-claim relations + applicability + query-conditioned temporal labels + roles + sufficiency + risk as a first-class intermediate representation. (2) The 'later timestamp does not prove supersession' thesis is empirically supported but unexploited: recency bias in LLM rerankers (2509.11353), corpus-sensitivity of recency priors (2509.19376), and MemStrata's failure on messy prose (44% supersession reliability) all show the field lacks a semantic, metadata-grounded superseding judgment - QVF's SUPERSEDES vs CONTRADICTS vs COEXISTS distinction fills this. (3) Conflict typology is impoverished: surveys distinguish only context-memory/inter-context/intra-memory; RAMDocs distinguishes only ambiguity vs misinformation vs noise. QVF's 9-relation set (esp. CONDITIONALLY_COMPATIBLE, COMPLEMENTS, SUPERSEDES-vs-CONTRADICTS) is finer-grained than anything published; a taxonomy-alignment table would be a strong related-work contribution. (4) Sufficiency+abstention is decoupled from conflict handling everywhere except Chen et al. 2022's calibration (which has no structure) - QVF unifies them. (5) Temporal QA benchmarks assume evidence is pre-scoped or gold; TempRAGEval is the only diagnostic per-evidence protocol, and none covers conversational memory. LongMemEval's temporal-reasoning/knowledge-update/abstention categories are the natural home, and no published LongMemEval system reports a structured validity-map intermediate - QVF would be first. (6) Naturally-occurring vs synthetic conflicts: most benchmarks perturb synthetically (entity substitution, ClashEval-style edits); Kortukov et al. and Open-Domain-QA-with-Conflicting-Contexts show behavior differs on real documents - QVF's use of real retrieved memories with real metadata is a defensible realism claim. (7) Risk flags (e.g., flagging that a memory is a DISTRACTOR or that supersession is UNRESOLVED) have no direct precedent; the closest is FreshQA's strict-mode 'no outdated statement anywhere' judging, which could be adapted into a stale-content-leakage metric for QVF.

summary:
The 2023-2026 literature on post-retrieval evidence processing splits into six strands, and across all of them the key finding for QVF is: many systems insert SOMETHING between retrieval and generation, but almost nothing inserts a typed, claim-level, query-conditioned validity structure, and temporal applicability is handled either globally (index-time supersession) or not at all.

(1) Self-reflective / corrective filtering. Self-RAG (ICLR 2024) is the canonical structured-signal approach: it trains an LM to emit reflection tokens — Retrieve, ISREL (is the passage relevant), ISSUP (is the output supported), ISUSE (utility) — making per-passage critique an explicit, discrete intermediate signal. CRAG (2024) inserts a lightweight T5-based retrieval evaluator that buckets retrieved documents into Correct / Incorrect / Ambiguous, triggers web-search fallback for bad buckets, and runs a decompose-then-recompose step to strip irrelevant spans. Both operate at document/passage granularity with relevance-or-correctness labels only: no inter-evidence relations, no temporal reasoning, no query-conditioned validity (a document is judged "correct" absolutely, not "correct for this query's time frame"). RankRAG (NeurIPS 2024) unifies context ranking and generation in one instruction-tuned LLM (Llama3-RankRAG-70B beats GPT-4 on nine knowledge-intensive benchmarks) — again pure relevance. FILCO (2023) trains sentence-level context filters using entailment, lexical overlap, and conditional cross-mutual information (CXMI), cutting prompt length up to 64%. NLI-based reranking/filtering is common but empirically mixed: naive NLI-only reranking degrades EM/F1; hybrid DPR+BM25+NLI works better; NLI checkpoints are widely used for span-level support detection. SEER (2024) learns self-aligned evidence extraction. InstructRAG (2024/ICLR 2025) has the model write explicit denoising rationales; Speculative RAG (2024/ICLR 2025) drafts answers+rationales in parallel from document subsets and verifies with a generalist LM.

(2) Claim decomposition. FActScore (EMNLP 2023) established the decompose-into-atomic-facts-then-verify paradigm; WICE (2023) does sub-claim entailment; VeriScore (2024) extracts only verifiable claims with a sliding context window; Core (2024) adds informativeness-weighted subclaim dedup; DnDScore (2024/EMNLP 2025) shows decontextualization must accompany decomposition; "Decomposition Dilemmas" (NAACL 2025) shows decomposition can boost OR burden verification. This strand supplies QVF's atomic-claim machinery but is used for output factuality evaluation, not as an input-side pre-generation structure, and none of it conditions claim validity on the query.

(3) Structured intermediate representations. StructRAG (ICLR 2025) is the flagship: at inference time a hybrid structure router picks the optimal structure type (table, graph, algorithm, catalogue, chunk) for the task, a structurizer converts raw retrieved documents into that structure, and a utilizer decomposes the question against it — proving that inference-time restructuring of retrieved evidence pays off on knowledge-intensive reasoning, but its structures carry no validity or temporal semantics. Chain-of-Note (2023/EMNLP 2024) generates per-document reading notes (direct-answer / inferential / unknown) before answering (+1.97 EM avg) — a textual, untyped precursor of QVF's memory roles. Astute RAG (2024) clusters internal+external knowledge into consistent vs conflicting groups and picks the most reliable cluster — a coarse structured grouping. CARE-RAG (2025) builds parameter-aware vs context-aware evidence representations and does conflict-driven summarization with a distilled 3B detector. Evidence/claim graphs exist mainly for fact-checking and multi-hop QA: FactCG (2025) uses graph-based multi-hop data for fact verification; Reasoning-with-Graphs (2025) extracts explicit reasoning graphs from context; GRS-QA (2024) provides reasoning-structure-annotated QA; a 2026 "Typed Claim Network" paper builds corpus-level typed claim networks for scientific literature; GraphRAG-style systems retrieve triples/subgraphs instead of passages. Compression is the degenerate case of intermediate structuring: RECOMP (ICLR 2024) does extractive/abstractive summarization of retrieved docs; LLMLingua/LongLLMLingua/LLMLingua-2 (2023-2024) do token-level pruning (LongLLMLingua is query-aware); a 2026 paper reframes soft compression as a "query-conditioned selector" — the phrase exists, but only for token selection, not validity.

(4) Sufficiency and evidential force. "Sufficient Context" (Google, ICLR 2025) introduces an autorater for whether retrieved context alone suffices to answer, showing big models answer wrongly instead of abstaining under insufficient context, and lifting selective accuracy 2-10 points; this is the direct precedent for QVF's SUFFICIENT/INSUFFICIENT/AMBIGUOUS field but is a single binary signal, not integrated with per-claim structure. "Relevant Is Not Warranted" (2026) argues relevance must be separated from evidential force in cited RAG — conceptually parallel to QVF's DIRECT_SUPPORT vs BACKGROUND vs DISTRACTOR roles.

(5) Knowledge conflicts. Contradiction Detection in RAG Systems (2025) evaluates LLMs as "context validators" over retrieved sets; WikiContradict (NeurIPS 2024 D&B) benchmarks real Wikipedia contradictions; ConflictBank (2024) covers context-memory and inter-context conflict at scale; DRAGged into Conflicts (2025) contributes the expert-annotated CONFLICTS benchmark with a conflict-type taxonomy and shows explicit reasoning about conflict type improves responses; MAGIC (2025) probes multi-hop graph-based inter-context conflicts; informing models of conflict type can add ~24 accuracy points. Crucially, these taxonomies classify conflicts (inter-context vs context-memory vs ambiguity) rather than assigning query-conditioned validity labels to each evidence item, and resolution strategies are mostly "prefer majority / prefer reliable cluster / surface both" rather than QVF-style per-claim adjudication.

(6) Temporal validity and memory-side neighbors (closest to QVF, mostly 2025-2026). Temporal RAG work largely bakes time into the index: T-GRAG/TG-RAG/DyG-RAG/E2RAG build timestamped or event-centric temporal graphs; SAT-Graph RAG does structure-aware temporal retrieval; IA-RAG (2026) applies Allen interval algebra for temporal reasoning over dynamic knowledge; ChronoQA and a Nature Scientific Data temporal-sensitive RAG dataset provide benchmarks. MemStrata ("Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory", 2026) implements a deterministic (subject, relation, object) supersession ledger that retires contradicted values with no LLM calls, cutting stale-fact errors from 15-40% to ~0% — but it is GLOBAL invalidation: once superseded, a fact is retired for all queries, exactly the assumption QVF rejects (a superseded fact is still CURRENT_FOR_QUERY for a historical question). "Don't Ask the LLM to Track Freshness" (2026) similarly argues for deterministic memory-conflict resolution. On the agent-memory side: STALE (2026) benchmarks whether agents know memories are no longer valid (400 conflict scenarios, 1200 queries; best models only 55.2%), and its CUPMem prototype adjudicates state at WRITE time; MemConflict (2026) explicitly frames memory validity as a "query-conditioned fitness-for-use problem" with dynamic (temporal), static (factual), and conditional (contextual) conflict categories — the closest conceptual framing to QVF, but it is a benchmark/diagnosis, not a structured representation. MemChain (2026) is the closest structural neighbor: a trainable post-retrieval policy that converts (query + retrieved memories) into a question-conditioned evidence plan plus an ordered grounded evidence trace organizing memories by semantic roles and dependencies, trained with SFT then trace-guided RL, achieving SOTA on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S with reduced context — but it optimizes answer quality end-to-end and does not emit interpretable validity labels, temporal applicability labels, typed inter-claim relations, or sufficiency/risk assessments.

Bottom line on the survey question: proposed structured intermediates include reflection/critique tokens (Self-RAG), correctness buckets (CRAG), reading notes (Chain-of-Note), extractive/abstractive summaries (RECOMP, compression), router-selected structures like tables/graphs (StructRAG), consistent-vs-conflicting clusters (Astute RAG, CARE-RAG), evidence/claim/reasoning graphs (FactCG, RwG, GraphRAG, typed claim networks), drafts+rationales (Speculative RAG, InstructRAG), sufficiency labels (Sufficient Context), and evidence plans/traces with semantic roles (MemChain). None of them jointly models query-conditioned applicability AND query-conditioned temporal validity at the atomic-claim level with typed inter-claim relations; temporal handling where it exists is index-time or globally deterministic, and query-conditioned validity exists only as a benchmark framing (MemConflict) or an implicit learned policy (MemChain), never as an explicit, interpretable output schema.

papers.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
papers.core_idea: Trains an LM to emit discrete reflection tokens (Retrieve, ISREL relevance, ISSUP support, ISUSE utility) that critique each retrieved passage and its own output, enabling adaptive retrieval and self-critique.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Earliest widely-adopted structured per-passage signal between retrieval and generation; labels are relevance/support/utility only — no inter-evidence relations, no temporal or query-conditioned validity semantics. QVF generalizes its per-passage critique into a full typed validity map.

papers.title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation (CRAG)
papers.core_idea: A lightweight T5-large retrieval evaluator scores retrieved documents into Correct/Incorrect/Ambiguous, triggers web-search fallback on failure, and a decompose-then-recompose algorithm strips irrelevant spans before generation.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Prototype of a post-retrieval validity gate, but document-level, three-way, and query-agnostic in time: 'correct' is absolute, whereas QVF labels are conditioned on the query's temporal/semantic frame and are claim-level with citations.

papers.title: RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs
papers.core_idea: Instruction-tunes a single LLM to do both context ranking and answer generation; a small fraction of ranking data in the training blend beats dedicated rankers; Llama3-RankRAG-70B outperforms GPT-4 on nine knowledge-intensive benchmarks.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Pure relevance ranking fused into the generator; no explicit intermediate representation at all — the opposite design point from QVF's interpretable external map.

papers.title: Learning to Filter Context for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (FILCO)
papers.core_idea: Trains sentence-level context filters using entailment, lexical overlap, and conditional cross-mutual information (CXMI); improves six knowledge-intensive tasks while cutting prompt length up to 64%.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Query-aware evidence selection at sentence granularity, but output is just a filtered string — discards rather than labels, and has no notion of conflicting/superseded/historical evidence.

papers.title: Chain-of-Note: Enhancing Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
papers.core_idea: Generates sequential reading notes for each retrieved document (direct-answer / inferential / unknown) before synthesizing the final answer; +1.97 EM average; supports 'unknown' abstention.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Free-text precursor of QVF's memory roles and sufficiency output, but notes are untyped prose with no schema, no citations-to-claims mapping, no relations between documents, no temporal labels.

papers.title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
papers.core_idea: Compresses retrieved documents into concise extractive or abstractive summaries before generation; can selectively augment (return empty summary when retrieval is useless).
papers.relation_to_qvf: Lossy textual compression as intermediate; the empty-summary option is a crude sufficiency signal. No structure, labels, or temporal reasoning.

papers.title: LLMLingua / LongLLMLingua / LLMLingua-2
papers.core_idea: Token-level prompt compression via small-LM perplexity (up to 20x); LongLLMLingua adds query-aware coarse-to-fine compression to fight lost-in-the-middle; LLMLingua-2 reformulates as token classification.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Query-aware but purely surface-level token pruning; retains no semantics about validity, conflict, or time. Shows the cost-reduction motivation QVF can also claim (compact validity map vs raw memories).

papers.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
papers.core_idea: Decomposes long-form generations into atomic facts and computes the fraction supported by a knowledge source (decompose-then-verify pipeline).
papers.relation_to_qvf: Source of QVF's atomic-claim granularity, but applied to output evaluation, not input structuring; verification is binary supported/unsupported with no query conditioning or claim-to-claim relations.

papers.title: Core: Robust Factual Precision with Informative Sub-Claim Identification / WICE / VeriScore / DnDScore / Decomposition Dilemmas
papers.core_idea: Claim-decomposition refinements: WICE does sub-claim entailment; VeriScore extracts only verifiable claims; Core deduplicates and weights sub-claims by informativeness; DnDScore couples decontextualization with decomposition; Decomposition Dilemmas (arXiv 2411.02400) shows decomposition can help or hurt verification.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Provides the technical toolbox (and pitfalls) for QVF's claim extraction step — especially the decontextualization requirement, which for QVF must preserve memory metadata (timestamps, session) so claims stay adjudicable.

papers.title: StructRAG: Boosting Knowledge Intensive Reasoning of LLMs via Inference-time Hybrid Information Structurization
papers.core_idea: A hybrid structure router picks the optimal structure type (table, graph, algorithm, catalogue, chunk) per task; an LLM structurizer converts retrieved documents into that structure; a utilizer decomposes questions against it. SOTA on knowledge-intensive reasoning.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Strongest evidence that inference-time restructuring between retrieval and generation works; but its structures encode content organization, not validity — no applicability, temporal, conflict, or sufficiency semantics. QVF can cite it as the structural paradigm and differentiate on label semantics.

papers.title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
papers.core_idea: Defines and auto-rates whether retrieved context alone is sufficient to answer; shows large models answer wrongly instead of abstaining when context is insufficient; sufficiency-guided abstention lifts selective accuracy 2-10 points; shipped in Vertex AI RAG Engine.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Direct precedent for QVF's SUFFICIENT/INSUFFICIENT/AMBIGUOUS field, but it is a single query-level binary signal detached from any claim structure; QVF integrates sufficiency with per-claim roles and risk flags.

papers.title: Astute RAG: Overcoming Imperfect Retrieval Augmentation and Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs
papers.core_idea: Elicits internal knowledge, then iteratively consolidates internal+external evidence by clustering into consistent vs conflicting groups and answering from the most reliable cluster; robust under worst-case retrieval.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Its consistent/conflicting clustering is a coarse two-relation ancestor of QVF's nine-relation taxonomy; conflict resolution is by cluster reliability, not query-conditioned adjudication, and there is no temporal dimension.

papers.title: Speculative RAG: Enhancing Retrieval Augmented Generation through Drafting
papers.core_idea: A small specialist LM drafts multiple answer+rationale pairs in parallel from distinct retrieved-document subsets; a generalist LM verifies and selects by rationale confidence.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Rationales are an implicit intermediate representation per evidence subset; perspective diversity across subsets loosely echoes QVF's COEXISTS/CONTRAST, but nothing is typed or query-conditioned.

papers.title: InstructRAG: Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Self-Synthesized Rationales
papers.core_idea: Trains the model to generate explicit denoising rationales connecting retrieved documents to answers, using self-synthesized rationale data.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Explicit denoising as free-text rationale; QVF replaces free-text rationale with an auditable typed schema.

papers.title: SEER: Self-Aligned Evidence Extraction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.core_idea: Learns evidence extraction aligned to the generator's own preferences (self-alignment) to select faithful, complete, relevant evidence spans.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Query-aware evidence selection optimized for downstream answer quality; extraction-only, no labels or relations.

papers.title: Contradiction Detection in RAG Systems: Evaluating LLMs as Context Validators
papers.core_idea: Frames the LLM as a 'context validator' that must detect contradictions inside retrieved document sets before generation; evaluates detection across contradiction types.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Validates QVF's premise that a dedicated validation pass over retrieved context is needed; detection-only — no resolution labels, no temporal or applicability dimensions.

papers.title: DRAGged into Conflicts: Detecting and Addressing Conflicting Sources in Search-Augmented LLMs (CONFLICTS benchmark)
papers.core_idea: Proposes a taxonomy of knowledge-conflict types in RAG with desired model behavior per type, and CONFLICTS, the first expert-annotated conflict-type benchmark in a realistic RAG setting; explicit reasoning about conflict type significantly improves responses.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Empirical support for QVF's design: making conflict type explicit helps generation. Its taxonomy classifies the conflict, while QVF labels each claim's validity for the query — complementary granularity.

papers.title: WikiContradict: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Real-World Knowledge Conflicts from Wikipedia
papers.core_idea: QA benchmark built from real intra-Wikipedia contradictions (including temporal ones) to test how models answer under inter-context conflict.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Useful stress-test material; shows real-world conflicts are often temporal — but offers no mechanism, only evaluation.

papers.title: MAGIC: A Multi-Hop and Graph-Based Benchmark for Inter-Context Conflicts in RAG
papers.core_idea: Knowledge-graph-derived benchmark for inter-context conflicts requiring multi-hop reasoning to even detect the conflict.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Motivates QVF's relation edges between claims: conflicts are often indirect (via chains), which flat per-document classifiers miss.

papers.title: Rethinking All Evidence: Enhancing Trustworthy RAG via Conflict-Driven Summarization (CARE-RAG)
papers.core_idea: Builds parameter-aware evidence (from internal knowledge) and context-aware evidence (refined retrieval), then a distilled 3B detector performs conflict-driven summarization before generation; includes a QA-repair step for outdated benchmark answers.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Closest RAG-side pipeline shape to QVF (refine → detect conflict → structured synthesis → generate), but its intermediate is a summary, not a labeled map, and 'outdated' is handled by fixing gold answers, not by query-conditioned temporal labels.

papers.title: Sufficient/temporal-graph line: RAG Meets Temporal Graphs; T-GRAG; DyG-RAG; TG-RAG; E2RAG; SAT-Graph RAG; IA-RAG
papers.core_idea: Family of temporal RAG systems that organize knowledge into timestamped subgraphs, event units, hierarchical temporal graphs, or dual entity-event graphs; IA-RAG (arXiv 2606.06044) adds Allen interval-algebra reasoning; SAT-Graph RAG does structure-aware temporal retrieval.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Temporality is baked into the INDEX/retrieval structure, resolved before or during retrieval; QVF instead adjudicates temporal applicability at read time conditioned on the query, requiring no re-indexing of memory stores.

papers.title: Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory (MemStrata): Eliminating Stale-Fact Errors for AI Agents over Evolving Knowledge
papers.core_idea: A deterministic (subject, relation, object) supersession rule over a bi-temporal ledger retires contradicted values without LLM calls; stale-fact error drops from 15-40% (RAG) to ~0%; notes cosine similarity separates contradiction from duplication at AUROC 0.59 (near chance).
papers.relation_to_qvf: The strongest anti-thesis to QVF: global, write-time, deterministic invalidation. It cannot serve historical queries with superseded facts — exactly the query-conditioned distinction QVF claims. Also supplies a great motivating statistic (embedding similarity cannot detect contradiction).

papers.title: STALE: Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid? (+ CUPMem)
papers.core_idea: Benchmark of 400 expert-validated implicit-conflict scenarios (1,200 queries, contexts to 150K tokens) testing state resolution, false-premise resistance, and implicit policy adaptation; best models reach only 55.2%. CUPMem prototype adjudicates state at write time via structured state consolidation.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Quantifies the failure QVF targets — models cannot implicitly track memory validity — and its premise-resistance dimension maps to QVF's risk flags; but its fix is write-time consolidation, whereas QVF is read-time and query-conditioned.

papers.title: MemConflict: Evaluating Long-Term Memory Systems Under Memory Conflicts
papers.core_idea: Frames memory validity as a query-conditioned fitness-for-use problem; formalizes dynamic (temporal), static (factual), and conditional (contextual) conflicts; multi-session dialogue benchmark with cross-session conflicts and semantic distractors; six systems show uneven strengths and degradation with history length and conflict distance.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Closest conceptual framing to QVF — literally 'query-conditioned fitness-for-use' — but it is a benchmark/diagnosis with no proposed representation or module; QVF can be positioned as the first method-side answer to MemConflict's diagnosis.

papers.title: MemChain: Learning Interpretable Memory Traces for Memory-Augmented LLM Agents
papers.core_idea: Trainable post-retrieval memory policy that converts (query + retrieved memories) into a question-conditioned evidence plan, an ordered grounded evidence trace organizing memories by semantic roles and dependencies, and explicit memory actions producing a compact evidence context; SFT + Trace-Guided Memory Policy Optimization (RL); SOTA on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S with frozen answer models.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Closest structural neighbor and the paper QVF must differentiate from: same insertion point (post-retrieval, pre-generation), same benchmarks. Differences: MemChain's roles/traces are learned and answer-optimized without a fixed interpretable schema; it has no temporal-applicability labels, no typed inter-claim relation taxonomy, no explicit sufficiency/risk output, and no query-conditioned validity semantics (a superseded memory is dropped, not labeled HISTORICAL_FOR_QUERY).

papers.title: Don't Ask the LLM to Track Freshness: A Deterministic Recipe for Memory Conflict Resolution
papers.core_idea: Argues LLMs should not adjudicate freshness at inference; proposes deterministic metadata-based rules for resolving memory conflicts.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Represents the deterministic-rules camp; QVF's counterargument is that timestamp rules alone conflate 'newer' with 'superseding' and cannot serve historical or conditional queries — the semantic adapter is needed precisely where rules underdetermine validity.

papers.title: Relevant Is Not Warranted: Evidence-Force Calibration for Cited RAG
papers.core_idea: Separates topical relevance from evidential force (whether a document actually warrants the cited claim) and calibrates citation strength accordingly.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Independent support for QVF's role taxonomy distinguishing DIRECT_SUPPORT from BACKGROUND/CORROBORATION/DISTRACTOR — relevance and support are different axes.

papers.title: FactCG: Enhancing Fact Checkers with Graph-Based Multi-Hop Data / Reasoning with Graphs (RwG) / GRS-QA
papers.core_idea: Claim/evidence-graph line: FactCG trains fact-checkers with graph-connected multi-hop synthetic data; RwG (arXiv 2501.07845) extracts explicit reasoning graphs from context before answering; GRS-QA (arXiv 2411.00369) annotates QA pairs with explicit reasoning-structure graphs.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Evidence graphs as intermediates exist for verification and multi-hop QA, but edges are reasoning/entailment dependencies, not validity relations; none are query-conditioned or temporal.

papers.title: Contextual Compression in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
papers.core_idea: Surveys hard (token-pruning) and soft (embedding) compression of retrieved context, covering LLMLingua family, RECOMP, and selective augmentation.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Useful related-work citation to bound the compression strand; confirms no surveyed compressor carries validity semantics.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Conflicting Evidence (RAMDocs / MADAM-RAG)
papers.core_idea: Dataset and multi-agent debate method for RAG where sources legitimately disagree (ambiguity, misinformation, noise); models must surface all valid answers while suppressing misinformation.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Its 'multiple valid answers can coexist' stance matches QVF's COEXISTS/CONDITIONALLY_COMPATIBLE relations; resolution is via agent debate rather than an explicit validity map.

sota_numbers: RankRAG: Llama3-RankRAG-70B outperforms GPT-4 on nine knowledge-intensive benchmarks (NeurIPS 2024 paper, https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/db93ccb6cf392f352570dd5af0a223d3-Abstract-Conference.html). Chain-of-Note: +1.97 EM average over standard RALM (arXiv 2311.09210). FILCO: outperforms baselines on six tasks while cutting prompt length up to 64% (arXiv 2311.08377). Sufficient Context: +2-10 points selective accuracy at fixed coverage via sufficiency-guided abstention (arXiv 2411.06037, ICLR 2025). Conflict-type awareness: informing LLMs of the conflict type present improves accuracy by ~24 percentage points (reported in inter-context conflict literature around MAGIC/CONFLICTS, arXiv 2507.21544 / 2506.08500). STALE: best frontier models only 55.2% overall accuracy on implicit memory-conflict scenarios (arXiv 2605.06527). MemStrata: stale-fact error ~0% vs 15-40% for vanilla RAG on evolving knowledge; cosine similarity separates contradiction from duplication at AUROC 0.59 (arXiv 2606.26511). MemChain: reported SOTA on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S with frozen answer models while substantially reducing memory context (arXiv 2607.24097). CRAG: retrieval-evaluator-triggered correction recovers 2-3 F1 points under query errors and degrades gracefully under adversarial retrieval noise where Self-RAG fails catastrophically (per emergentmind summary of arXiv 2401.15884 follow-ups).
gaps_for_qvf: 1) No existing structured intermediate representation jointly encodes atomic claims with memory-ID citations + typed inter-claim relations + query-conditioned applicability + query-conditioned temporal labels + memory roles + sufficiency + risk flags. Existing intermediates are one-dimensional: relevance tokens (Self-RAG), correctness buckets (CRAG), notes (Chain-of-Note), summaries (RECOMP/CARE-RAG), content structures (StructRAG), consistent/conflicting clusters (Astute RAG), or learned traces (MemChain). 2) Temporal applicability is either index-time (temporal graph RAG: T-GRAG/TG-RAG/DyG-RAG/IA-RAG) or global write-time supersession (MemStrata, CUPMem, deterministic-freshness recipes); no system emits read-time labels like HISTORICAL_FOR_QUERY vs SUPERSEDED_FOR_QUERY — the 'old memory is correct for a historical question' and 'later timestamp does not prove supersession' distinctions are explicitly unmodeled, and MemStrata's global retirement is provably wrong for historical queries. 3) Query-conditioned validity exists only as a benchmark framing (MemConflict's 'query-conditioned fitness-for-use') and as an implicit learned objective (MemChain); no method outputs it as an interpretable schema — QVF can position itself as the first method-side, schema-explicit answer to the MemConflict/STALE diagnosis. 4) Conflict work (CONFLICTS, WikiContradict, MAGIC, ConflictBank) shows conflict-type awareness helps (~24 pts) but stops at detection/taxonomy; QVF's relation taxonomy (EQUIVALENT…SUPERSEDES…CONDITIONALLY_COMPATIBLE) plus per-claim adjudication is the missing resolution layer. 5) Sufficiency (Sufficient Context) is a query-level binary detached from claim structure; QVF integrates sufficiency with the evidence map so INSUFFICIENT/AMBIGUOUS verdicts are attributable to specific missing or conflicting claims. 6) Differentiation risks to manage in the paper: MemChain (2607.24097) occupies the same insertion point and same benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S) — QVF must emphasize interpretable fixed schema, temporal/applicability labels, zero-training LLM-adapter design, and auditability; and the deterministic camp (MemStrata, 'Don't Ask the LLM to Track Freshness') will argue LLM adjudication is unnecessary — QVF should include cases where deterministic rules underdetermine validity (historical queries, conditional facts, corroboration vs update) and cite MemStrata's own AUROC 0.59 embedding result as evidence that semantic adjudication is required.
benchmark_details: Not a benchmark-focused area, but conflict/temporal evaluation resources found: CONFLICTS (arXiv 2506.08500) — expert-annotated conflict types in realistic search-augmented settings; WikiContradict (arXiv 2406.13805) — QA over real Wikipedia contradictions; MAGIC (arXiv 2507.21544) — KG-derived multi-hop inter-context conflicts; ConflictBank — large-scale Wikidata-based conflict claims; RAMDocs (arXiv 2504.13079) — documents with ambiguity/misinformation/noise; STALE (arXiv 2605.06527) — 400 scenarios / 1,200 queries / contexts to 150K tokens, three-dimension validity evaluation; MemConflict (arXiv 2605.20926) — multi-session dialogues with dynamic/static/conditional conflicts and distractors; ChronoQA — 5,176 Chinese temporal questions over 300K news articles (2019-2024); temporal-sensitive RAG QA dataset in Nature Scientific Data 2025 (arXiv 2508.12282).

Primary arXiv PDFs are at the /abs/ URLs listed per paper.

summary:
The novelty check shows that QVF's problem space — deciding, per query, whether retrieved memories are valid, applicable, and temporally current — has become an active 2025-2026 research area, but no existing system produces QVF's proposed artifact: a single structured "Query-Conditioned Validity Map" combining atomic claims with memory-ID citations, a 9-way inter-claim relation taxonomy, per-query applicability labels, per-query temporal labels, memory roles, sufficiency assessment, and risk flags.

The exact conceptual framing QVF uses already appears in the literature. MemConflict (arXiv 2605.20926) explicitly "treats memory validity as a query-conditioned fitness-for-use problem" and decomposes it into temporal validity, factual correctness, and contextual applicability — but it is a diagnostic BENCHMARK (controlled multi-session dialogues with injected cross-session conflicts and distractors), not a method; it evaluates six existing memory systems and finds answer correctness misaligned with retrieval quality. STALE (arXiv 2605.06527) benchmarks whether agents know their memories are no longer valid (400 expert-validated conflict scenarios, 1,200 queries, up to 150K-token contexts; three probes: State Resolution, Premise Resistance, Implicit Policy Adaptation; best model only 55.2%); its companion method CUPMem works at WRITE time via state consolidation, not at read time conditioned on the query. These two are strong motivation/evaluation resources rather than competing methods.

On the method side, three works occupy nearly the same pipeline slot as QVF (after retrieval, before generation). ConvMemory v3 (arXiv 2606.26753) is the closest in spirit: a "Validity Context Layer" doing target-conditioned relation verification between retrieval and generation, evaluated on LongMemEval and LoCoMo — but its validity assessment is conditioned on the target proposition/entity and centers on supersession verification, without QVF's full relation taxonomy, per-query temporal label set (e.g., HISTORICAL_FOR_QUERY vs SUPERSEDED_FOR_QUERY vs FUTURE_OR_NOT_YET_VALID), memory roles, sufficiency, or risk flags. MemChain (arXiv 2607.24097) is a TRAINED post-retrieval policy (SFT + RL/TMPO) that emits question-conditioned evidence plans (with temporal scope current/recent/historical/any) and grounded evidence traces with evidence roles, citations, and relations, plus KEEP/DROP/MERGE/REFINE/ADD actions; it reports 69.80% on LoCoMo (GPT-4.1-mini answerer, +6.10 over the strongest baseline) and evaluates LongMemEval-S. MemChain's goal is token-efficient evidence compression optimized for answer reward, not an interpretable, declarative validity adjudication with explicit UNKNOWN/abstention labels — but it is the work QVF most needs to differentiate from in a related-work section, since "question-conditioned plan + roles + relations + citations between retrieval and a frozen generator" overlaps heavily. DeferMem (arXiv 2605.22411, query-time evidence distillation via RL) and RaMem (arXiv 2606.22844, validity-aware contextual reinstatement) are adjacent in the same slot.

The opposite design pole is deterministic, query-INDEPENDENT validity: MemStrata ("Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory," arXiv 2606.26511) maintains a bi-temporal ledger with (subject, relation)-keyed supersession, no LLM on the read path, ~0% stale-fact errors vs RAG's 15-40%, and archives superseded facts for as-of-time queries; "Don't Ask the LLM to Track Freshness" (arXiv 2606.01435) similarly argues for deterministic conflict-resolution rules (evaluated on MemoryAgentBench). These works validate QVF's premise that timestamp-only heuristics fail, but their validity is decided at ingestion, globally — directly contrasting QVF's thesis that validity is only well-defined relative to the query. In classic RAG filtering, Corrective RAG (arXiv 2401.15884) grades retrieved documents Correct/Incorrect/Ambiguous per query, Astute RAG consolidates conflicting internal/external knowledge, MADAM-RAG/RAMDocs (arXiv 2504.13079) handles conflicting evidence with multi-agent debate, and ECoRAG compresses by evidentiality — all coarser than QVF (document-level relevance or conflict handling, no temporal-applicability semantics, no structured map). Knowledge-conflict benchmarks (ConflictBank, WikiContradict, DRAGged into Conflicts arXiv 2506.08500) cover the CONTRADICTS relation only.

Acronym check: "QVF" has no discovered collision with any ML system, model, or benchmark. It does collide outside ML with (1) the Qlik Sense application file format .qvf (widely known in BI/analytics) and (2) Michigan's "Qualified Voter File" official voter-registration database. Neither blocks use in an ML paper, but search-engine noise will be dominated by Qlik; consider styling as "QVF (Query-conditioned Validity Filter)" consistently.

papers.title: MemConflict: Evaluating Long-Term Memory Systems Under Memory Conflicts
papers.core_idea: Diagnostic benchmark that treats memory validity as a query-conditioned fitness-for-use problem; formalizes dynamic (temporal), static (factual), and conditional (contextual-applicability) conflicts; builds controlled multi-session dialogues with cross-session conflicts and semantically similar distractors; evaluates six memory systems via black-box answer accuracy plus white-box retrieval/ranking analysis.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Shares QVF's exact conceptual framing (query-conditioned validity, three of QVF's label dimensions) but is a BENCHMARK, not a method: it measures failures, proposes no adapter, no structured validity map, no relation taxonomy, no memory roles, no sufficiency/risk output. It is the strongest evidence the problem is recognized — and an additional evaluation target QVF should consider using. QVF must cite it and position itself as the first structured-output method for the problem MemConflict measures.

papers.title: ConvMemory v3: A Validity Context Layer for Conversational Memory via Target-Conditioned Relation Verification
papers.core_idea: Inserts a validity verification layer between memory retrieval and generation that performs target-conditioned relation verification: supersession/validity of a stored fact is judged relative to the target proposition being asked about, and only validity-passing memories reach the generator; evaluated on LongMemEval and LoCoMo.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Closest method overall: same pipeline slot (post-retrieval, pre-generation), same insight that validity is conditional rather than global, same two benchmarks QVF plans. Differences: its conditioning is on the target entity/proposition rather than the full query (so it cannot distinguish a historical-intent query from a current-intent query about the same target); it verifies a narrow relation set centered on supersession rather than QVF's 9-way relation taxonomy; it outputs a filtered memory set, not a declarative map with per-query applicability labels, per-query temporal labels (HISTORICAL_FOR_QUERY, FUTURE_OR_NOT_YET_VALID, etc.), memory roles, sufficiency assessment, or risk flags. QVF must differentiate explicitly from this paper.

papers.title: MemChain: Learning Interpretable Memory Traces for Memory-Augmented LLM Agents
papers.core_idea: Trainable post-retrieval memory policy (SFT + trace-guided RL) that generates a question-conditioned evidence plan (including temporal scope: current/recent/historical/any), a grounded evidence trace with evidence roles, candidate-ID citations and inter-step relations, and KEEP/DROP/MERGE/REFINE/ADD actions, then hands a compact evidence context to a frozen answer model; 69.80% on LoCoMo, evaluated also on LongMemEval-S, with ~24x context compression.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Heaviest overlap in output structure: question-conditioned planning, roles, relations, and citations between retrieval and a frozen generator, on QVF's exact benchmarks. Differences: MemChain is a TRAINED small-model policy optimized end-to-end for answer reward and token compression; its labels are actions and loose roles, not a normative validity taxonomy; it has no query-conditioned applicability/temporal label semantics, no explicit UNKNOWN/abstention labels, no sufficiency or risk-flag output, and its artifact is a compressed evidence packet rather than an auditable validity map. QVF's contribution must be framed as the declarative, interpretable, prompt-based (Claude-backend) adjudication layer with calibrated abstention — not another compression policy.

papers.title: STALE: Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid? (with CUPMem)
papers.core_idea: Probing benchmark for memory-validity awareness: 400 expert-validated conflict scenarios / 1,200 queries across 100+ topics with contexts up to 150K tokens; tests State Resolution, Premise Resistance, and Implicit Policy Adaptation; best frontier model reaches only 55.2%. Companion prototype CUPMem strengthens write-time revision via structured state consolidation and propagation-aware search.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Provides the empirical motivation QVF needs (a large retrieve-vs-act-on-validity gap) and introduces implicit conflicts (invalidation without explicit negation), which QVF's CONTRADICTS/SUPERSEDES/CONDITIONALLY_COMPATIBLE relations should handle. Differences: it is a benchmark plus a WRITE-time consolidation method; QVF operates at READ time conditioned on the query, so an old memory can remain valid for a historical question — a case write-time state overwriting handles poorly. STALE's premise-resistance probe also suggests an extension QVF lacks: flagging false presuppositions in the query itself.

papers.title: Temporal Validity in Retrieval Memory: Eliminating Stale-Fact Errors for AI Agents over Evolving Knowledge (MemStrata)
papers.core_idea: Deterministic supersession layer: bi-temporal ledger (valid_from/valid_to/superseded_by) with (subject, relation)-keyed structural supersession decided at ingestion, no LLM or similarity threshold on the read path; superseded facts archived for as-of-time queries; drives stale-fact answer rate from RAG's 15-40% to ~0% on evolving-knowledge benchmarks, and shows embeddings cannot separate contradictions from paraphrases (AUROC 0.59).
papers.relation_to_qvf: The design antithesis of QVF and a key contrast citation. Its validity is global and query-independent, fixed at write time by ingestion order over structured triples; QVF's central claim is that validity is only defined relative to the query and that a later timestamp alone does not prove supersession — precisely the semantic judgment MemStrata refuses to make (its LLM fallback exists only for non-triple prose). MemStrata cannot express partial applicability, conditional compatibility, corroboration vs distraction, or sufficiency; conversely, its determinism/latency argument is a critique QVF must answer (QVF adds an LLM call per query on the read path). Its impossibility result for embedding-based conflict detection is strong supporting evidence for QVF's semantic-adapter approach.

papers.title: Don't Ask the LLM to Track Freshness: A Deterministic Recipe for Memory Conflict Resolution
papers.core_idea: Argues LLM-judged freshness is unreliable and proposes deterministic rules for resolving memory conflicts, evaluated on MemoryAgentBench; acknowledges older memories can be correct for retrospective queries.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Adjacent contrast work in the same deterministic camp as MemStrata; shares QVF's observation that newer-is-not-always-better, but resolves conflicts with rules rather than producing query-conditioned semantic labels, relations, roles, or sufficiency. Useful as a baseline/ablation reference (deterministic rules vs QVF's semantic adapter).

papers.title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation (CRAG)
papers.core_idea: A retrieval evaluator grades retrieved documents as Correct/Incorrect/Ambiguous per query, filters noise via decompose-then-recompose, and triggers corrective web search when retrieval fails.
papers.relation_to_qvf: The canonical ancestor of query-conditioned post-retrieval filtering in RAG. Differences: document-level 3-way relevance grading with no temporal semantics, no inter-evidence relations, no memory metadata, no roles, and a corrective-action objective rather than a structured validity representation. QVF generalizes this slot from relevance to validity/applicability/temporality over personal agent memory.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Conflicting Evidence (MADAM-RAG / RAMDocs)
papers.core_idea: Benchmark (RAMDocs) and multi-agent debate method (MADAM-RAG) for RAG under conflicting, ambiguous, and noisy retrieved documents, distinguishing legitimate ambiguity from misinformation.
papers.relation_to_qvf: Representative of the RAG knowledge-conflict line (with ConflictBank, WikiContradict, DRAGged into Conflicts arXiv:2506.08500, Astute RAG, Micro-Act arXiv:2506.05278). Covers essentially only QVF's CONTRADICTS relation and does so over web documents without timestamps/metadata; no temporal labels, applicability, roles, or sufficiency, and resolution happens via debate rather than an explicit declarative map. QVF should cite this line as handling one cell of its taxonomy.

sota_numbers: STALE: best frontier model only 55.2% overall accuracy on memory-validity probing (arXiv:2605.06527). MemChain: 69.80% accuracy on LoCoMo with GPT-4.1-mini answerer, +6.10 pts over strongest baseline, evidence context 143.3 tokens vs 3,491 for baselines; also evaluated on LongMemEval-S (500 instances) (arXiv:2607.24097). MemStrata: stale-fact answer rate ~0% vs 15-40% for vanilla RAG on evolving-knowledge suites; 0.95-1.00 vs 0.20-0.47 accuracy on code/config/API-evolution benchmarks; embedding AUROC 0.59 (near chance) for contradiction-vs-duplicate detection; read latency ~2.1s vs ~16-18s for LLM-rerank baselines (arXiv:2606.26511). MemConflict: six memory systems show uneven performance across dynamic/static/conditional conflict types, with answer correctness frequently misaligned with supporting-memory retrieval quality (arXiv:2605.20926). Graphiti temporal KG reports 94.8% vs MemGPT 93.4% on Deep Memory Retrieval (vendor-reported, vectorize.io/mem0 blog).
gaps_for_qvf: (1) No existing system emits a declarative, auditable Query-Conditioned Validity Map: prior work either benchmarks the problem (MemConflict, STALE), filters/compresses without interpretable validity semantics (MemChain, DeferMem, ConvMemory v3), or decides validity deterministically and query-independently at write time (MemStrata, freshness-recipe). QVF's combined artifact — atomic claims + citations + 9-way relation taxonomy + per-query applicability + per-query temporal labels + memory roles + sufficiency + risk flags — has no direct precedent. (2) Query-conditioned TEMPORAL semantics are unclaimed territory: no found system distinguishes HISTORICAL_FOR_QUERY from SUPERSEDED_FOR_QUERY or has FUTURE_OR_NOT_YET_VALID; MemChain's temporal scope (current/recent/historical/any) is the nearest but is a plan attribute, not a per-memory label. (3) The explicit principle "a later timestamp alone does not prove supersession" contradicts the deterministic camp's ingestion-order rule and is empirically supported by STALE's implicit-conflict findings — a defensible, testable thesis. (4) Calibrated abstention via UNKNOWN labels and sufficiency assessment (SUFFICIENT/INSUFFICIENT/AMBIGUOUS) is absent from all found post-retrieval methods; CRAG's Ambiguous label is the only coarse analog. (5) Memory-role assignment (DISTRACTOR, CORROBORATION, QUALIFIER, etc.) as an explicit output is novel; MemChain has looser evidence roles inside traces. (6) Open attack surfaces QVF must defend: latency/cost of an LLM adapter call on the read path (MemStrata's critique), and differentiation from ConvMemory v3 (same slot, same benchmarks) and MemChain (similar structured intermediate) — the paper should include deterministic-rule and compression-policy baselines. (7) Evaluation gap QVF can exploit: MemConflict and STALE provide conflict-focused test beds where no structured-map method has yet been reported; adding one of them beyond LongMemEval/LoCoMo would strengthen novelty claims. Acronym: no ML collision found for "QVF"; collisions exist outside ML (Qlik Sense .qvf file format; Michigan Qualified Voter File) — usable but expect search noise.
